   965:   int32_t scissor_bottom = int32_t(scissor.offset[1] + scissor.extent[1]);
   966:   x0 = std::clamp(x0, int32_t(scissor.offset[0]), scissor_right);
   967:   y0 = std::clamp(y0, int32_t(scissor.offset[1]), scissor_bottom);
   968:   x1 = std::clamp(x1, int32_t(scissor.offset[0]), scissor_right);
   969:   y1 = std::clamp(y1, int32_t(scissor.offset[1]), scissor_bottom);
   970: 
   971:   assert_true(x0 <= x1 && y0 <= y1);
   972: 
   973:   // Direct3D 9's D3DDevice_Resolve internally rounds the right/bottom of the
   974:   // rectangle internally to 8. While all the alignment should have already been
   975:   // done by Direct3D 9, just for safety of host implementation of resolve,
   976:   // force-align the rectangle by expanding (D3D9 expands to the right/bottom
   977:   // for some reason, haven't found how left/top is rounded, but logically it
   978:   // would make sense to expand to the left/top too).

   980:   y0 &= ~int32_t(xenos::kResolveAlignmentPixels - 1);

   982:   y1 = xe::align(y1, int32_t(xenos::kResolveAlignmentPixels));

   992:     return false;
   993:   }

  1002:   rb_surface_info.msaa_samples =

  1005:   // Clamp to the EDRAM surface pitch (maximum possible surface pitch is also
  1006:   // assumed to be the largest resolvable size).
  1007:   int32_t surface_pitch_aligned =
  1008:       int32_t(rb_surface_info.surface_pitch &
  1009:               ~uint32_t(xenos::kResolveAlignmentPixels - 1));

  1012:            x1, surface_pitch_aligned);

  1014:     x1 = std::min(x1, surface_pitch_aligned);

We need an independent, adversarial GPU/emulator engineering answer to a stuck Blue Dragon/Xenos->Vulkan placement problem.

Target: xenia fork, Blue Dragon field, AYN Thor Adreno 740, Mesa Turnip TBDR. Goal 30fps. Device-proven dead: every per-publish copy, blit, shader convert, or separate resolve causes GMEM traffic and collapses to 1.8-2fps. The only viable architecture is: each producer renders directly into a persistent resource-keyed native Vulkan render target, later composite samples the same native resource, and Xenos EDRAM ownership transfers are dropped.

The current blocker is exact placement of a predicated 2-tile fan-out into ONE logical 1280x720 native RT. Confirmed from registers + RenderDoc:
- Left tile group: PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET=0, intended logical coverage x=[0,672], y=[0,720].
- Right tile group: nonzero window offset (historically -608), intended logical coverage x=[608,1280], y=[0,720].
- overlap x=[608,672] is intended.
- Wide post-VS positions / NDC and clipping mean variants that globally ignored PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET all failed.
- Two ordered draw groups share the same color+depth surface: viewport width 1280 first, then width 672; both depth LessEqual + write.
- Field uses 2x/4x MSAA in portions; mixed-resolution bloom/composite elsewhere.
- Prior whole-frame native attempt striped. Three “ignore window offset” variants are dead. Overriding RB_SURFACE_INFO.surface_pitch black-screens.

Current xenia mechanics:
1) draw_util::GetHostViewportInfo:
- if PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL.vtx_window_offset_enable and not draw_ignore_window_offset, adds signed PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET to the guest viewport offset.
- for clip-enabled draws this affects BOTH returned VkViewport bounds and ndc_scale/ndc_offset constants used by translated shaders; therefore ignoring early may alter host clip/crop behavior.
2) draw_util::GetScissor:
- starts PA_SC_WINDOW_SCISSOR_TL/BR;
- adds PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET iff TL.window_offset_disable==0;
- intersects screen scissor;
- by default clamps x to RB_SURFACE_INFO.surface_pitch.
3) Vulkan UpdateDynamicState emits those viewport/scissor values.
4) The failed whole-frame native path additionally replaces every native draw scissor with full 1280x720. This likely lets each tile replay leak outside its intended tile.
5) The newer color producer substitution at VulkanCommandProcessor::SubmitBarriersAndEnterRenderTargetCacheRenderPass around line 4695 only swaps framebuffer handle. GetBdNativeColorProducerFramebuffer allocates native image and framebuffer at base->host_extent, e.g. tile-rounded 1280x2048, and Submit uses framebuffer->host_extent for renderArea. The consumer descriptor swaps only the view, while shader UVs remain logical [0,1], so it samples the empty tail.
6) Once a Vulkan VkImage is bound, guest EDRAM tiling/addressing is not used for fragment addressing; raster writes by Vulkan framebuffer coordinates. RB_SURFACE_INFO still feeds cache identity, sample count, EDRAM fallback, resolve math, and scissor clamp.
7) Existing source already has an unused NativeRasterBinding concept with window offsets, resolve source x/y, and destination x/y. The persistent resolve graph maps full RenderTargetKey -> destination resource, but ResolveEdge currently lacks full source/destination rectangles.

Candidate fix to red-team:
- Make native image/framebuffer logical 1280x720, keep RB_SURFACE_INFO unchanged.
- Keep PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET honored through GetHostViewportInfo so translated shader NDC/clip compensation remains identical.
- Do NOT widen scissor and do NOT replace viewport width.
- After normal Xenos-to-host viewport/scissor calculation, translate the final raster window from tile-local to logical coordinates. For known BD mapping, tile delta = -window_offset: left delta 0; right window=-608 -> delta +608. Add delta to final VkViewport.x. Add delta to final scissor offset only when window offset was applied to the window scissor; retain extent. Intersect with 1280x720. Thus right tile local [0,672] becomes logical [608,1280] without changing ndc_scale/offset or frustum decisions.
- More robustly, record at resolve time per resource/tile: local source rect and logical destination rect, and use delta = destOrigin-srcOrigin rather than assuming -window_offset.
- Use one shared logical color+depth target and preserve draw order; not two tile images.
- For MSAA, use a multisampled transient GMEM color attachment plus a single-sample logical resolve attachment via pResolveAttachments in the same render pass, MSAA store DONT_CARE, resolve STORE+SAMPLED. Composite samples resolve view. Never vkCmdResolveImage/separate pass. Potentially use VK_EXT_multisampled_render_to_single_sampled only if feature-proven.
- Direct mode must skip current Seed/Mirror vkCmdCopyImage, otherwise it violates the proven no-copy architecture.

Questions:
A) Is the post-calculation viewport/scissor translation mathematically and semantically correct, and why is it different from early “ignore window offset”?
B) Could stripes instead be Xenos tiled-address mapping after binding a logical VkImage?
C) Should one logical image or per-tile images be used?
D) Exact MSAA design on Turnip / whether pResolveAttachments is an on-tile no-extra-pass resolve.
E) Concrete xenia changes at the line-4695 substitution and GetBdNativeColorProducerFramebuffer, including extent metadata, renderArea, dynamic state, depth, resource mapping, and which registers must stay unchanged.
F) Identify hidden failure modes: PA_SC_WINDOW_SCISSOR_TL.window_offset_disable, vtx_window_offset_enable, viewport/scissor clamping order, overlap depth semantics, mixed sample counts, render-pass compatibility, descriptor texture dimensions, and pass breaks.

Do not flatter. Be specific and technical. Treat device measurements as ground truth.

scratch\thor-debug\codex_edram.md:5018:ROAA is the right primitive for ordered in-place programmable blend on the current attachment. Vulkan defines it as implicit framebuffer-local ordering between previous color attachment writes and current input-attachment reads, enabling shader-side custom blending in rasterization order. It should map to GMEM-style attachment access on a tiler, but the spec guarantee is ordering/local attachment semantics, not a promise of physical GMEM residency. It does not survive render-pass breaks and does not help arbitrary transformed texture coordinates. See Khronos ROAA and dynamic local-read semantics: ([registry.khronos.org](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/man/html/VK_EXT_rasterization_order_attachment_access.html)) ([docs.vulkan.org](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPipelineColorBlendStateCreateFlagBits.html)) ([docs.vulkan.org](https://docs.vulkan.org/features/latest/features/proposals/VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering_local_read.html)).
scratch\thor-debug\codex_edram.md:5020:`VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering_local_read` is useful as a dynamic-rendering version of subpass/local-read scheduling, not as a universal texture-cache replacement. Its storage-resource local-read rule is keyed to overlapping fragment locations, so it still does not make “consumer pixel samples producer pixel at transformed coordinate” GMEM-local. `VK_EXT_attachment_feedback_loop_layout` makes same-subresource render+sample legal, but arbitrary sampled feedback is likely to force sysmem behavior or defeat tiler locality; it is a correctness tool, not the main performance primitive. `VK_EXT_shader_tile_image` would be closer to what you want for tile attachment reads, but it is absent and is still pixel-location based. ([registry.khronos.org](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/man/html/VK_EXT_attachment_feedback_loop_layout.html)) ([registry.khronos.org](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/man/html/VK_EXT_shader_tile_image.html))

    BD GMEM-residency foundation (brick 2): Stage-0 resource-graph data model
    
    Adds the NativeResourceKey / NativeResourceVersion / NativeRasterBinding types
    (5.6-sol GMEM-residency design). These describe a BD surface by RESOURCE identity
    (base_address/guest_pitch/logical dims/format/endian/mip/layer) - NOT the base-
    aliased EDRAM RenderTargetKey - so native RTs don't alias and no ownership
    transfers are needed. NativeResourceVersion adds the generation + exact resolve
    rect (resolve_dest alone is insufficient: addresses reused, many-to-many).
    NativeRasterBinding retains guest pitch/window-offset ONLY for mapping BD's tile
    strips into the full-surface native image. Shared vocabulary for the foundation;
    wired by the resource-graph populate + early-RTC-selection bricks next. Compiles.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+  // GMEM-residency foundation Stage-0 data model (5.6-sol design 2026-07-11,
+  // docs/research/20260711-gmem-residency-pass-fusion-30fps-56sol.txt). These

    BD GMEM-residency foundation (brick 3): populate the native resource graph
    
    At each guest resolve (IssueCopy), record a NativeResourceVersion keyed by guest
    base_address (many versions per base for reuse + the bloom pyramid), built from
    RESOURCE identity (base/pitch/logical-dims/format/endian) - not the base-aliased
    EDRAM key. RecordNativeResourceVersion bumps the matching key's generation or
    appends. NativeResourceVersionsForBase() reads it back. Read-only recording -
    does NOT change rendering (safe, additive); the early-RTC-selection brick will
    consult this to pick the exact native producer generation to bind. Compiles.
    NEXT: early RTC selection (native binding decision before RenderTargetCache::
    Update) + field custom resolve (on-tile MSAA) - the render-path integration.

diff --git a/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_command_processor.h b/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_command_processor.h
index a4e7b1b5a..67d011f29 100644

   // is retained for back-compat callers.
   std::unordered_map<uint32_t, std::vector<ResolveEdge>>
       persistent_resolve_edge_versions_;
+  // GMEM-residency foundation (brick 3): the native RESOURCE graph - every resolve
+  // recorded as a versioned NativeResourceVersion keyed by guest base address
+  // (many versions per base: reuse + the bloom pyramid). Populated at resolve
+  // time from RESOURCE identity (not EDRAM tile identity). Read-only recording;
+  // the early-RTC-selection brick will consult it to pick the native producer.
+  std::unordered_map<uint32_t, std::vector<NativeResourceVersion>>
+      native_resource_versions_;
+
+ public:
+  // Record a resolve's native resource version (foundation graph population).
+  // Bumps the generation of a matching key in place, or appends a new one.
+  void RecordNativeResourceVersion(const NativeResourceKey& key, uint32_t rect_x,
+                                   uint32_t rect_y, uint32_t rect_w,
+                                   uint32_t rect_h) {
+    if (!key.base_address) {
+      return;
+    }
+    auto& versions = native_resource_versions_[key.base_address];
+    for (NativeResourceVersion& v : versions) {
+      if (v.key == key) {
+        ++v.generation;
+        v.dest_rect_x = rect_x;
+        v.dest_rect_y = rect_y;
+        v.dest_rect_w = rect_w;
+        v.dest_rect_h = rect_h;
+        return;
+      }
+    }
+    if (versions.size() < 16) {
+      NativeResourceVersion v;
+      v.key = key;
+      v.generation = 1;
+      v.dest_rect_x = rect_x;
+      v.dest_rect_y = rect_y;
+      v.dest_rect_w = rect_w;
+      v.dest_rect_h = rect_h;
+      versions.push_back(v);
+    }
+  }
+  // All native resource versions recorded at a guest base (or nullptr).
+  const std::vector<NativeResourceVersion>* NativeResourceVersionsForBase(
+      uint32_t base_address) const {
+    auto it = native_resource_versions_.find(base_address);
+    return it == native_resource_versions_.end() ? nullptr : &it->second;
+  }
+
+ private:
   // Per-frame attribution of render-pass breaks at the per-draw enter point:
   // _barrier = ended to flush a pending barrier; _rt_change = ended because the
   // render pass / framebuffer changed (RT reconfiguration).

## Verdict

Use one logical `1280×720` native color image plus one shared logical depth image. The placement transform is:

1. Let Xenia apply `PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET` normally while calculating shader NDC compensation and tile-local viewport/scissor.
2. After that calculation, translate the resulting raster window from tile-local coordinates into logical-resource coordinates.
3. Never replace the per-tile scissor with a full-screen scissor.

For the confirmed BD pair:

| Group | Window offset | Local→logical delta | Final logical coverage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Left | `0` | `0` | `[0,672)` |
| Right | `-608` | `+608` | `[608,1280)` |

So the right transform is not “ignore the offset” and not “apply the raw offset again.” It is: honor `-608` during Xenia’s clip/NDC conversion, then add `+608` to the final Vulkan viewport/scissor placement.

### 1. Exact placement

Xenia’s offset-ignore variants changed too much. `GetHostViewportInfo` incorporates the window offset before producing both the host viewport and translated-shader `ndc_scale/ndc_offset`; removing it there can therefore change clipping. That matches the RenderDoc result where primitives disappear at the frustum. See [draw_util.cc](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/draw_util.cc:365>).

Do this instead:

```cpp
draw_util::draw_ignore_window_offset = false;
draw_util::GetHostViewportInfo(..., viewport_info);

// Construct normal VkViewport from viewport_info first.
VkViewport viewport = ...;

// Do not clamp a logical native target to the guest tile-strip pitch.
draw_util::Scissor scissor;
draw_util::GetScissor(regs, scissor,
                      /*clamp_to_surface_pitch=*/false);

auto mode = regs.Get<reg::PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL>();
auto woff = regs.Get<reg::PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET>();
auto ws_tl = regs.Get<reg::PA_SC_WINDOW_SCISSOR_TL>();

// Prefer the learned resolve mapping:
int32_t dx = binding.dest_offset_x - binding.resolve_src_x;
int32_t dy = binding.dest_offset_y - binding.resolve_src_y;

// BD-specific validated fallback:
// dx = mode.vtx_window_offset_enable ? -woff.window_x_offset : 0;
// dy = mode.vtx_window_offset_enable ? -woff.window_y_offset : 0;

if (mode.vtx_window_offset_enable) {
  viewport.x += float(dx);
  viewport.y += float(dy);
}

// GetScissor applied PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET only when this bit is clear.
if (!ws_tl.window_offset_disable) {
  scissor.offset[0] += dx;
  scissor.offset[1] += dy;
}

// Intersect the translated scissor with [0,1280)x[0,720).
ClampScissorToExtent(scissor, logical_extent);
```

Keep `viewport.width`, `viewport.height`, and `viewport_info.ndc_*` unchanged. The translation must happen after `GetHostViewportInfo`, so hardware raster placement moves without changing the translated clip positions.

The register roles are explicit in [registers.h](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/registers.h:610>):

- `PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL.vtx_window_offset_enable`: whether the offset affects vertex/window placement.
- `PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET`: signed 15-bit X/Y offsets.
- `PA_SC_WINDOW_SCISSOR_TL.window_offset_disable`: independently controls whether the offset affects the window scissor.
- `RB_SURFACE_INFO.surface_pitch`: guest EDRAM pitch, not the logical native-image width.

### 2. Why `whole_frame` striped

There are two concrete problems in that experiment.

First, the native path currently overwrites every tile scissor with the entire native extent at [vulkan_command_processor.cc](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_command_processor.cc:9996>). That removes the tile mask selecting which part of the wide replay belongs to each group. With the wide NDC geometry, both replays leak outside their intended regions and interfere through color and depth—exactly the shape that can produce stripes.

Second, the older `BdNativeRenderer` render pass orders attachments as color-then-depth, while the RTC’s guest render pass orders depth first and colors afterward. Compare [bd_native_renderer.cc](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/bd_native_renderer.cc:687>) with [vulkan_render_target_cache.cc](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:2195>). That render pass is not compatible with the translated guest pipelines, so its desktop result and Adreno failure are not clean evidence against the logical-image design.

This is not a Xenos raster-addressing problem. Once a `VkImage` is bound as an attachment, fragments write by Vulkan framebuffer `(x,y)` coordinates; Turnip’s internal optimal tiling is opaque. `RB_SURFACE_INFO` can still corrupt keying, MSAA selection, scissor clamping, or fallback resolve math, but it does not remap native pixels into an Xenos tile-strip address.

Use:

- `renderArea = {0,0,1280,720}`
- translated per-group viewport/scissor
- no global viewport-width override
- no full-scissor override

### 3. One image versus per-tile images

One logical image is correct.

Both groups intentionally share color, depth, ordering, and the `[608,672)` overlap. Splitting into two images loses the shared `LessEqual + Z-write` behavior in the overlap and then requires either a reassembly pass, extra sampler logic, or a copy—all inferior here.

The correct sequence is:

1. Bind one `1280×720` color/depth pair.
2. Render the `vpw=1280` group.
3. Render the `vpw=672` group without clearing or replacing depth.
4. Resolve once, after both groups.
5. Sample the resulting logical image with the composite’s existing `[0,1]` UVs.

### 4. MSAA on Turnip

The ordinary composite cannot sample a 4× image through its existing normalized, filtered `sampler2D`. Direct multisample access requires a multisampled image type, integer texel coordinates, explicit sample indices, and shader-side reduction.

Use an in-render-pass resolve:

- N-sample logical color attachment.
- Matching N-sample depth.
- Single-sample `1280×720` resolve attachment.
- `pResolveAttachments` on the producer subpass.
- MSAA color `storeOp = DONT_CARE`, ideally transient/lazily allocated.
- Resolve image `storeOp = STORE`, final layout shader-read.
- No `vkCmdResolveImage`.

That resolve is part of subpass completion, not a separate pass. On tilers it lets the implementation resolve in tile memory while writing the final 1× image; Khronos explicitly recommends this over a separate resolve because the latter materializes and rereads the multisampled attachment. [Khronos MSAA guidance](https://docs.vulkan.org/samples/latest/samples/performance/msaa/README.html), [TBR guidance](https://docs.vulkan.org/guide/latest/tile_based_rendering_best_practices.html).

Two caveats:

- It removes off-chip MSAA materialization, not MSAA raster/depth work or its larger GMEM footprint.
- If the composite remains a later normal texture-sampling pass, the 1× result still has to be stored and then sampled. Literal cross-pass GMEM residency is only possible by fusing the composite as a subpass/local read, and only for framebuffer-local access—not arbitrary neighboring/filtered UV reads. Mesa documents Turnip’s GMEM-versus-sysmem model here: [Freedreno/Turnip architecture](https://docs.mesa3d.org/drivers/freedreno.html).

Your Turnip exposes `VK_EXT_multisampled_render_to_single_sampled` at [bd_residency_boot_utf8.log](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/scratch/thor-debug/bd_residency_boot_utf8.log:209>). That may ultimately be ideal, but Xenia currently does not enable/query its feature. Classic `pResolveAttachments` is the smaller first implementation. A single-subpass resolve variant can remain pipeline-compatible when the original color/depth references and attachment indices are preserved; Vulkan explicitly ignores resolve-reference differences for single-subpass render-pass compatibility. [Vulkan render-pass compatibility](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/renderpass.html).

### 5. Concrete Xenia changes

The final direct path cannot remain a late line-4695 attachment substitution.

Current structural problems:

- `GetBdNativeColorProducerFramebuffer` caches its image on an EDRAM-keyed framebuffer entry, so multiple logical resources reusing the same EDRAM configuration alias one native image.
- It allocates from `base->host_extent` at [vulkan_render_target_cache.cc](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:3490>).
- The native graph currently sets `dest_width = RB_SURFACE_INFO.surface_pitch` at [vulkan_command_processor.cc](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_command_processor.cc:8799>), recreating the tile-strip/logical-size confusion.
- `written_address` is the resolve extent start, not necessarily the canonical texture-resource base, at [vulkan_render_target_cache.cc](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:1786>).
- Line 4695 is after pass/framebuffer equality handling, so two native resources sharing one LLE framebuffer can be mistaken for the same active pass.

Required shape:

1. Before `RenderTargetCache::Update`, select a `NativeBindingPlan` from the packed source RT key and the prior-frame resolve graph.

2. Canonicalize the resource using the consumer `TextureKey`:

   - canonical base address;
   - logical width/height;
   - format/mip/layer;
   - generation.

   Use `RB_COPY_DEST_PITCH.copy_dest_pitch/height` as the resolve-side fallback, not `RB_SURFACE_INFO.surface_pitch`; its fields are defined at [registers.h](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/registers.h:887>).

3. Populate the existing `NativeRasterBinding` with full, uncompressed rectangles:

   ```text
   local source rect -> logical destination rect
   delta = destination.origin - source.origin
   ```

   Keep `PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET` and scissor values as validation/fingerprint data. Don’t rely solely on `-window_offset`, even though it matches the confirmed BD right group.

4. Cache native images by `NativeResourceKey`, and cache framebuffer wrappers by approximately:

   ```text
   {native resource/generation, compatible render pass, depth view, samples}
   ```

   The wrapper extent is logical `1280×720`; it must not be cached on the LLE framebuffer alone.

5. At pass begin:

   - bind the stable logical framebuffer wrapper;
   - use logical extent for `renderArea`;
   - use a correctly ordered compatible resolve render-pass variant for MSAA;
   - set `bd_native_direct_active_`;
   - skip `SeedBdNativeColorProducer`;
   - skip `MirrorBdNativeColorProducer`;
   - publish the single-sample native view directly to the resource alias.

6. Leave `RB_SURFACE_INFO` untouched. Its guest pitch/MSAA remain necessary for source-RT identity, pipeline selection, and the EDRAM fallback. Only bypass its horizontal scissor clamp while the logical native target is active.

7. Initially, the oversized LLE depth view may be attached to a smaller logical framebuffer—Vulkan permits attachment images larger than the framebuffer. The completed no-ownership path should use a resource-keyed logical depth image too, because the two groups must retain the same depth contents and remain in one pass.

The decisive capture invariant is simple: unchanged post-VS/clip output versus LLE, final dynamic scissors exactly `[0,672)` and `[608,1280)`, one color view, one depth view, and no clear/pass break between the two groups. If those are true and the producer image is correct but the composite is garbled, placement is solved and the remaining fault is strictly the sampled view/resolve extent or descriptor generation.

The `consult-hard` second-opinion path could not run because this read-only session prevented the local Codex client from creating its temporary app-server directory; the conclusions above come from the current source, captured facts, Mesa documentation, and Vulkan specification.

## Verdict

Use one logical `1280×720` native color image plus one shared logical depth image. The placement transform is:

1. Let Xenia apply `PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET` normally while calculating shader NDC compensation and tile-local viewport/scissor.
2. After that calculation, translate the resulting raster window from tile-local coordinates into logical-resource coordinates.
3. Never replace the per-tile scissor with a full-screen scissor.

For the confirmed BD pair:

| Group | Window offset | Local→logical delta | Final logical coverage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Left | `0` | `0` | `[0,672)` |
| Right | `-608` | `+608` | `[608,1280)` |

So the right transform is not “ignore the offset” and not “apply the raw offset again.” It is: honor `-608` during Xenia’s clip/NDC conversion, then add `+608` to the final Vulkan viewport/scissor placement.

### 1. Exact placement

Xenia’s offset-ignore variants changed too much. `GetHostViewportInfo` incorporates the window offset before producing both the host viewport and translated-shader `ndc_scale/ndc_offset`; removing it there can therefore change clipping. That matches the RenderDoc result where primitives disappear at the frustum. See [draw_util.cc](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/draw_util.cc:365>).

Do this instead:

```cpp
draw_util::draw_ignore_window_offset = false;
draw_util::GetHostViewportInfo(..., viewport_info);

// Construct normal VkViewport from viewport_info first.
VkViewport viewport = ...;

// Do not clamp a logical native target to the guest tile-strip pitch.
draw_util::Scissor scissor;
draw_util::GetScissor(regs, scissor,
                      /*clamp_to_surface_pitch=*/false);

auto mode = regs.Get<reg::PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL>();
auto woff = regs.Get<reg::PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET>();
auto ws_tl = regs.Get<reg::PA_SC_WINDOW_SCISSOR_TL>();

// BD-specific validated fallback:
// dx = mode.vtx_window_offset_enable ? -woff.window_x_offset : 0;
// dy = mode.vtx_window_offset_enable ? -woff.window_y_offset : 0;

  viewport.x += float(dx);
  viewport.y += float(dy);
}

// GetScissor applied PA_SC_WINDOW_OFFSET only when this bit is clear.
if (!ws_tl.window_offset_disable) {
  scissor.offset[0] += dx;
  scissor.offset[1] += dy;
}

// Intersect the translated scissor with [0,1280)x[0,720).
ClampScissorToExtent(scissor, logical_extent);
```
